quotes.text: Music critic Robert Palmer once suggested Jarreau had created a remarkable vocal vocabulary in his throat, as a way of describing the breadth of sounds that come from it. A German writer, equally dazzled, suggested Jarreau has a whole orchestra in his pipes.

He found a guitar player and for the first time was doing music as a feature rather than incidental member of a trio. 'I found all of this room in which to create, accompany myself, and add to the music, improvise in away there had never been for: me before. I began to scat more and really open up to try a lot of different things.'

There was a lot of experimenting going on, but not in the laboratory sense. I never went to the back room and started cataloging the sounds or numbering them and noting how I did it. I was experimenting in a real practical performing sense, discovering there were places in the voice that I could go to.

I was doing, for many years, ti-ka, ti-ka, ti-ke, ti-ka, ti-ti-ti-ka-a-a-a, stuff like that, making vocal percussion sounds by myself and just fooling around, entertaining myself, driving in the car, walking down the street, being my own radio, It was fun, trying this and that once in a while.
Born in Milwaukee, just an hour from my home, I have a special sentiment for this brilliant mellow vocalist with a genuine talent for scatting in relatively pop friendly formats.
His voice is smooth, rivaling that of Johnny Mathis and Nat King Cole, only Jarreau has more cool funk and soul to his style.

Surrounding himself with superb studio musicians and under the capable guidance Jay Graydon, this album contains no bad selections, a rarity back in the 80s when most top 40 albums had maybe 2 good songs.
"Not Like This" is just stunning low-key pyrotechnics from a man who knows what he wants to do with his voice and makes it very unmistakably clear to your ears.

Check out the fact that, not only is this album perfect in material with some co-written by Jarreau himself, but the arrangements are produced to create a subtle, romantic, and effective backdrop that make the absolute most of featuring his smooth-as-cream voice.
Jarreau was clearly a man ahead of his time when it came to product placement.
